item.title: Walmart in Wiggins evacuated after ruptured gas line - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
WIGGINS – The Walmart Supercenter in Wiggins was evacuated early Monday after a ruptured gas line was reported outside the store, according to the Wiggins Fire Department.

Firefighters responded at about 3 a.m. to the store after reports of a gas line rupture.

When crews arrived, they confirmed the damaged line was outside the building and had been accidentally struck, the fire department said.

As a precaution, the store was evacuated.

The fire department said the Walmart Supercenter will remain closed until the gas line is repaired and the area is declared safe by the local gas company.

Wiggins Fire Department units remained on scene and on standby while repairs were underway.

Officials said Walmart will resume normal operations once the repairs are completed and the scene is cleared.

item.title: Tuesday Weather: Mix of clouds, possible storms - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Mary Apel
item.description:
Happy Tuesday morning, friends! It’s going to be a warm and somewhat unsettled day across the area, with highs climbing to around 82 degrees. Expect a mix of clouds and sunshine this morning, with isolated thunderstorms developing this afternoon. A few of those storms could turn strong to severe, so keep an eye on the sky if you have outdoor plans. South winds will be breezy at 10 to 15 mph.

Tonight, thunderstorms remain possible through the evening before tapering off after midnight, leaving behind mostly cloudy skies and a mild low near 68 degrees. Some storms could still be strong early on.

Looking ahead, we stay in an active weather pattern for much of the week. More scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms are possible Wednesday, then cooler air moves in Thursday with more clouds around.

Friday looks to be the wettest day of the stretch, with widespread rain likely and much cooler temperatures, only reaching the low 60s. A few leftover showers are possible Saturday morning, but the weekend improves nicely, with sunshine returning Sunday and temperatures rebounding into the mid-70s.

Overall, expect a stormy start to the week, a cooler and soggy finish to the workweek, and much nicer weather by the weekend.

item.title: Ridgeland PD asks public to help injured officer - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RIDGELAND — The Ridgeland Police Department is asking the public to help out an officer who was seriously injured in a crash along the Natchez Trace Parkway during severe weather Sunday morning, officials said.

Cpl. Ryan Stacy was involved in the crash April 26 when his vehicle struck a fallen tree on the Natchez Trace, according to the police department.

Authorities said Stacy had to be extricated from the vehicle and was taken to a local hospital, where he is being treated for serious injuries.

Police Chief Brian Myers said the department is asking for prayers for Stacy and his family as he recovers.

“The Ridgeland PD family asks for your prayers for a speedy recovery for Ryan and prayers for his family during this difficult time,” Myers said in a statement.

The department said Stacy faces a lengthy recovery and asked the community to keep him, his family and fellow officers in their prayers.

Stacy was recently recognized as Officer of the Month during the department’s March board meeting.

Support efforts for Stacy and his family are being coordinated through the 1828 Project of Madison County, according to the department.

item.title: National LawFit Challenge returning to DeSoto County in July - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
DESOTO COUNTY — Some of the nation’s fittest law enforcement officers will return to north Mississippi this summer for the 2026 National LawFit Challenge , a three-day competition focused on fitness, discipline and professional camaraderie.

The event is scheduled for July 16-18 in DeSoto County and will bring together officers from across the country to compete in a series of physical challenges designed to test strength, speed, flexibility and endurance.

The competition is hosted in Mississippi in part because of the state’s long-standing success in the event, according to Thomas Tuggle, the national LawFit coordinator. Founded in 2002, the competition has become a showcase for law enforcement fitness and preparedness.

Participants compete in events including bench press, pull-ups, sit-ups, a 1.5-mile run and a 200-yard agility course that simulates job-related tasks such as suspect apprehension, officer rescue, wall climbs and simulated shooting.

Tuggle has said the event promotes health, better decision-making and survival readiness for officers in high-risk situations, while also fostering friendships among competitors.

“It’s designed to test strength, speed, flexibility and endurance,” Tuggle said in past years. “They leave there with a newfound idea of what friendship is.”

Organizers say the competition highlights leadership and discipline while encouraging officers to set fitness goals and push themselves professionally and personally.

Mississippi has long fielded strong competitors in the event, with Tuggle previously saying the state’s performance helps counter stereotypes about law enforcement in the state.

Registration is now open for competitors, and organizers are also seeking sponsors for the 2026 event.

item.title: Mississippi joins multistate human trafficking operation that led to 4 arrests, recovery of 3 victims in Biloxi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
BILOXI – Mississippi participated in a nationwide human trafficking operation spanning 30 states that led to four arrests and the recovery of three victims in Biloxi, according to Attorney General Lynn Fitch.

Fitch said the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office Human Trafficking Task Force led the state’s role in Operation Coast to Coast, which was conducted April 23.

Nationally, the operation involved more than 250 law enforcement agencies and resulted in 59 arrests and the recovery of 166 victims, including 12 minors, according to the attorney general’s office.

“My office is committed to taking criminals who traffic people off our streets and equally committed to setting victims on the road to recovery,” Fitch said in a statement. “Developing partnerships with federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies both within Mississippi and across the country is a priority for the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office.”

The attorney general’s office said agencies involved in Mississippi included the Biloxi Police Department, FBI, Harrison County Sheriff’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Mississippi Bureau of Investigation and Mississippi Gaming Commission.

The Gulf Coast Center for Nonviolence provided services and treatment to the victims recovered during the operation, according to the attorney general’s office.

Operation Coast to Coast began in 2024 as an initiative of the Human Trafficking Training Center to encourage a broader national response to human trafficking, officials said.

The attorney general’s office said it has now trained 588 law enforcement officers statewide. It also said the office’s human trafficking team has led 63 multi-jurisdictional operations resulting in the recovery of 390 victims and 204 arrests, along with additional leads tied to trafficking investigations.

item.title: Mississippi Blood Services urges donors to give at Flowood, Oxford centers - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
FLOWOOD – Mississippi Blood Services is urging people to donate blood, saying donations are needed now more than ever to help patients across the community.

The organization said people can donate at its donor centers in Flowood and Oxford.

The Flowood Donor Center is located at 115 Tree St. and is open from 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. The Oxford Donor Center is located at 2627 W. Oxford Loop, Suite C, and is open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., according to Mississippi Blood Services.

Walk-ins are welcome, the organization said. People who want to schedule a donation ahead of time can call 601-368-2673.

Mississippi Blood Services is asking donors to bring a photo ID, eat well before donating and stay hydrated.

item.title: Mississippi Blood Services asks for platelet donations - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
FLOWOOD — Mississippi Blood Services is calling for immediate platelet donors as inventory has dropped to critically low levels, raising concerns about meeting patient needs statewide.

Officials said the organization needs to collect at least 40 platelet donations daily to supply partner hospitals across Mississippi.

Platelets are used to help control bleeding and support patients undergoing cancer treatment, major surgeries and emergency care. Because platelets expire within five days of donation, officials said maintaining a steady donor base is crucial.

“We need to collect 40 or more platelet donations daily to adequately supply our local hospital partners,” Kasey Dickson, the organization’s director of marketing and public relations, said in a statement.

Dickson said sickle cell patients and cancer patients of all ages rely on platelet products to continue lifesaving treatments.

“Without enough donors, those treatments — along with critical surgeries — can be delayed,” Dickson said.

Mississippi Blood Services is encouraging eligible donors to give as soon as possible. As an incentive, platelet donors will receive a $50 Visa gift card.

Donations are being accepted at the organization’s centers in Flowood, Cleveland and Oxford. The Flowood donation center, located at 115 Tree St., offers weekday and weekend hours, including Sunday appointments for platelet donations only. Centers in Cleveland and Oxford are also accepting donors during scheduled weekday hours.

Appointments can be made through Mississippi Blood Services or by phone, though walk-in donors are also welcome. Officials said additional donors are needed immediately to help prevent disruptions in care.

item.title: Mississippi Attorney General K9 Trace to Get Donation of Body Armor - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Today, Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced that K9 Officer TracE will receive a bullet and stab protective vest thanks to a charitable donation from non-profit organization Vested Interest in K9s, Inc. K9 TracE’s vest was sponsored by Eve R. Hershkowitz of Brielle, NJ and will be embroidered with the sentiment “Gifted by Eve R. Hershkowitz, Brielle, NJ”. Delivery is expected within ten weeks.

“Providing protective equipment to K9s like TracE ensures that our law enforcement dogs receive the same level of protection as the officers they serve alongside,” said Attorney General Fitch. “This donation will allow TracE to not only work effectively and confidently in high-risk situations, but ensure her safety and wellbeing when engaged in law enforcement activities. Thank you to Vested Interest and Ms. Hershkowitz for their generous gift.”

Vested Interest in K9s, Inc., established in 2009, is a 501(c)(3) charity whose mission is to provide bullet and stab protective vests and other assistance to dogs of law enforcement and related agencies throughout the United States. This potentially lifesaving body armor for four-legged K9 officers is U.S. made, custom fitted, and National Institute of Justice (NIJ) certified. Since its inception, Vested Interest in K9s, Inc. has provided over 6,397 vests valued at $6.9 million to K9s in all 50 states, made possible by both private and corporate donations.

The program is open to U.S. dogs at least 20 months old, actively employed, and certified with law enforcement or related agencies. K9s with expired vests are also eligible to participate. There are an estimated 30,000 law enforcement K9s throughout the United States.

Vested Interest in K9s, Inc. accepts tax-deductible contributions in any amount, while a single donation of $1,050 will sponsor one vest. Each vest has a value of $1,800.00, weighs an average of 4-5 lbs., and comes with a five-year warranty. For more information, or to learn about volunteer opportunities, please call (508) 824-6978. Vested Interest in K9s, Inc. provides information, lists events, and accepts donations at www.vik9s.org , or you may mail your contribution to P.O. Box 9, East Taunton, MA 02718.

You can learn more about Mississippi Attorney General K9 TracE by visiting attorneygenerallynnfitch.com/divisions/cyber-crime/ .

item.title: MHP investigates hit-and-run crash involving Lafayette County school bus - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LAFAYETTE COUNTY – The Mississippi Highway Patrol is investigating a hit-and-run crash involving a Lafayette County School District bus and a passenger vehicle on Highway 334, according to the Lafayette County Sheriff’s Department.

Deputies were dispatched to the crash at about 3:32 p.m. Monday, April 27, authorities said.

The sheriff’s department said the driver of the passenger vehicle left the scene before deputies arrived. No injuries were reported.

The Lafayette County Fire Department, Lafayette County Emergency Management Agency and Baptist Ambulance Service also responded to the scene, according to the release.

Investigators said the Mississippi Highway Patrol is leading the investigation with assistance from Lafayette County sheriff’s investigators. Authorities said detectives have identified a person of interest, but no name has been released.

Sheriff Joey East said the case will be pursued aggressively.

“The safety of our children and the men and women who drive them to school every day is non-negotiable,” East said in a statement. “In Lafayette County, there will be zero tolerance for anyone who puts our students or our bus drivers in harm’s way.”

No additional information was immediately released.

item.title: Man found dead in Jackson street, investigation underway - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Jackson police are investigating after an unresponsive man was found lying in a street Tuesday evening.

According to the Jackson Police Department, a Precinct 3 officer on routine patrol around 8:30 p.m. observed a person lying in the roadway. After checking on the individual, the officer found an unresponsive male, authorities said.

The man is believed to be about 42 years old, though investigators are still working to make a positive identification before notifying next of kin.

Police said the cause and manner of death have not yet been determined.

Detectives are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1800 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS.

item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
KEMPER COUNTY – The Kemper County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help locating a man wanted in connection with a shooting Monday at the Deville Apartment Complex.

Authorities identified the suspect as Antonio Lamont Johnson Jr., also known as “Lil Tony.”

The sheriff’s office said Johnson is wanted in connection with the shooting, which happened April 27 at the apartment complex.

Authorities warned the public not to approach Johnson if he is seen.

Anyone with information about his whereabouts is asked to contact the Kemper County Sheriff’s Office immediately at 601-743-2255 or call 911.

The sheriff’s office said all tips will remain confidential.

item.title: Jackson police investigating homicide on Abraham Lincoln Drive - Darkhorse Press

Precinct 3 officers responded on Tuesday to a report of an aggravated assault at a residence, where they discovered Jason Johnson lying on the floor with multiple gunshot wounds, according to the Jackson Police Department.

Investigators said Johnson died at the scene from his injuries.

Police said the shooting occurred during an altercation between Johnson and another individual. The suspect left the residence before officers arrived and has not been identified.

Members of the department’s Robbery/Homicide Unit and Mobile Crime Unit also responded to the scene and are leading the investigation.

No additional details about the suspect or circumstances surrounding the altercation were immediately released.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1800 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS.

item.title: Employee accused of stealing $7000 worth of items from storage unit - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
FLOWOOD — A Rankin County woman has been arrested and charged with embezzlement after authorities say she used her job at a storage facility to steal more than $7,000 worth of electronics from a customer’s unit.

Deputies and investigators with the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department responded Monday to Old Fannin Road Store & Lock, located on Old Fannin Road just outside Flowood, in reference to a reported theft.

According to investigators, Autumn Sanderford Eargle, an employee at the mini-storage facility, accessed a customer’s storage unit and removed multiple items, including Apple electronic products. The total value of the stolen property was estimated to exceed $7,000.

Eargle was arrested and charged with embezzlement. She was transported to the Rankin County Adult Detention Center in Brandon. During an initial court appearance Tuesday, Rankin County Court Judge David Morrow Jr. set Eargle’s bond at $25,000.

Authorities said the stolen property has been recovered and returned to its owner.

item.title: California man reported missing arrested in Jones County on outstanding felony warrants - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JONES COUNTY – A California man who had been reported missing was arrested Monday afternoon in Jones County after authorities located him driving on Interstate 59 and discovered he was wanted on several felony warrants.

Authorities said Aaron Kravetz, 39, of Montecito, California, was found driving a Volkswagen GTI north on I-59 near Exit 104 in the Sandersville area.

A Mississippi Department of Public Safety Commercial Transportation Enforcement Division officer located Kravetz, officials said. Additional units from the Sandersville Police Department, Mississippi Highway Patrol and Jones County Sheriff’s Department responded to the scene at the officer’s request.

In addition to being reported missing from Montecito, Kravetz had several outstanding felony warrants out of Santa Barbara County, California.

Those warrants include threats to commit a crime with intent to terrorize, stalking, contempt of court and four counts of disobeying a court order.

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: Latrice "Shay" Armstead, Coahoma County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
CRENSHAW — Latrice “Shay” Armstead’s sister said her jaw was wired shut when she disappeared, a symptom of an abusive relationship that plagued her and worried her family.

Her disappearance is still a mystery almost 14 years after her loved ones noticed she was gone.

According to investigators, Armstead had recently moved to St. Louis, Missouri, in an effort to escape the abusive relationship while filing for divorce. She left her three children with family members for their safety during the process. She returned to Memphis to retrieve her youngest son but disappeared before she could go back to Missouri.

Family members reported her missing on July 30, 2012, after she failed to check in with her children, which they say she did daily, often multiple times a day. The following day, her vehicle was found burned near Little Simmons Road in Clarksdale.

Originally from Crenshaw, she has not been seen or heard from since.

Armstead, 38, was last seen July 28, 2012, in Memphis, with her estranged husband, Tony Bledsoe. At the time of her disappearance, she was 5 feet 3 inches tall and weighed about 152 pounds, with black hair and brown eyes. She had pierced ears and several distinctive tattoos, including three bears on her left shoulder blade, a rosary around her left arm, a blue rose on her right arm, a panther on her leg and a heart on her left breast. Her jaw was wired shut after it had been broken in an alleged domestic assault.

Her case has since been classified as a cold case, but her family continues to push for answers. In a 2020 report by ABC 24, her sister, Brinda Armstead, described her as generous and deeply devoted to her family.

“Family-oriented — if she had something and you were a friend, it’s as good as yours,” Brinda Armstead told reporter Rebecca Butcher.

Her sister said it quickly became clear something was wrong when Armstead stopped calling.

“She would call quite often to check on her kids,” she said. “When I realized that I hadn’t heard from her … I really knew something was wrong.”

Brinda Armstead has publicly expressed suspicion toward Bledsoe, citing a history of alleged domestic abuse uncovered during the investigation. Authorities have said Armstead was last seen with him in Memphis.

“No one else around her that we know has motive,” she said in the ABC 24 report. “Everyone that the police wanted to question … came in without any fear or anything except for him.”

Investigators have never announced any arrests in the case.

Anyone with information about Latrice Armstead’s disappearance is urged to contact the Coahoma County Sheriff’s Department at 662-624-3085. Anonymous tips can also be submitted to Memphis CrimeStoppers at 901-528-CASH.

For Armstead’s family, the years without answers have been painful — but they have not given up hope.

“Given her personality and how she was,” her sister said, “people just don’t disappear.”

JACKSON – A 19-year-old man has been arrested and charged in connection with a fatal shooting Saturday night at Leavell Woods Park, according to the Jackson Police Department.

item.title: Ser Boxley featured in the Mississippi Encyclopedia - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
NATCHEZ – The Mississippi Encyclopedia now features a biographical entry on Ser Seshsh Ab Heter‑C. M. Boxley. The entry is a chronological and thematic overview of his life, highlighting his significant contributions to Natchez and Mississippi history as an activist, author, preservationist, and public historian.

The Mississippi Encyclopedia is published by the Center for the Study of Southern Culture at the University of Mississippi and has been funded by the Mississippi Humanities Council.

Dr. Stuart Rockoff, executive director of the Mississippi Humanities Council, said he was pleased to see Boxley featured in the publication.

“It is fitting for Ser Boxley to become part of the Mississippi Encyclopedia,” he said. “His commitment to preserving the story of the enslaved in Natchez and at Forks of the Road has blazed a trail in how we can tell a more honest and accurate story of our past.”

James G. Thomas, Jr., associate director for publications at the Center for the Study of Southern Culture, said he and his team were all happy to feature Ser Boxley in the Mississippi Encyclopedia.

The biographical entry focuses on Ser Boxley’s early life and family background, as well as his education and civil rights activism, which includes his role with the Natchez Deacons for Defense and Justice. It also covers his trips to Africa and the adoption of his African name.

Additionally, the entry features his major achievements as a historian and cultural preservationist. Those achievements include his decades-long work on the Forks of the Road slave market, which is now part of the National Park Service, and his creation of living history programs.

It also underscores his contributions as an author and the donation of his life’s work to the Mississippi Department of Archives and history.

The idea for the entry originated with Michael Morris, director of the Two Mississippi Museums in Jackson. It can be viewed at: https://mississippiencyclopedia.org/entries/boxley-ser-seshsh-ab-heter-c-m/

item.title: Opinion: Vital journalism is under stress - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
By Bill Crawford Syndicated Columnist

JACKSON — The Mississippi Press Association, celebrating its 160th anniversary, held a forum highlighting local journalism last week at History Is Lunch in the Two Museums.

MPA Vice President Peter Imes, publisher of the Commercial Dispatch in Columbus, spoke of the vital role local journalism “plays at the grassroots level in our democracy” as he welcomed the panel.

Charles Overby, chair of the Overby Center for Southern Journalism at Ole Miss, moderated. Panelists included professional journalists Natalie Perkins from the Deer Creek Pilot in Rolling Fork, Jamie Patterson from the Yazoo Herald in Yazoo City, and Anita Lee from the Sun Herald in Biloxi.

Discussion focused on local journalism’s importance as a community storyteller, watchdog and public information source.

All three speakers agreed local journalists provide essential benefits other media sources do not: preserving and documenting community stories with context and history; serving as watchdogs over local elected officials and government operations; covering routine civic life (city councils, school boards, etc.); and producing community-focused features that resonate locally.

Perkins noted the critical role her small newspaper played in communicating with local people after an EF4 tornado struck.

“We continue to tell the story,” she said, “and we’re the only ones that give a rip about Sharkey County.”

“Being a person that they go to church with or see in the grocery store or at the Little League field,” Patterson said, lets local people “know that I have just as much stake in the community as they do.”

The panelists also agreed on the persistent threats to local journalism from social media misinformation, ad revenue losses to online media and audience shifts, particularly among young people, to free online platforms.

“I’ve been very concerned about that for a while now,” Lee said, “and I try to do my little part, which is like spitting in the ocean, to assure people that I’m a real journalist. This is what I do and this is how I do it. So I just hope people are discerning and careful about what media they consume.”

Panelists expressed concern that local journalism is “in trouble” as staffing shrinks and dailies become bi-weeklies. But they remain optimistic if dedicated professional journalism persists and communities support local news outlets.

Lee stressed the latter, lamenting that people don’t realize their local news source is going to go away one day if local support dries up. They will have to depend upon social media alternatives that lack professional standards and commitments to fairness and transparency.

“I feel so horrible for those communities that are kind of in news deserts that don’t have those newspapers and don’t have those watchdogs. That’s scary,” Patterson concluded.

“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge” — Hosea 4:6.

Crawford is an author and syndicated columnist from North Jackson.

item.title: Mississippi rescue group takes in multiple dogs, helps pregnant dog deliver 10 puppies - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
MONTICELLO – Safe Haven Rescue MS says it spent a busy weekend responding to multiple calls for help, rescuing several dogs and caring for a mother dog that delivered 10 puppies.

According to the rescue, the weekend began Friday with a call about a small puppy found abandoned under a car. The group said the puppy, now named Winston, is about 6 weeks old and was heavily covered in fleas when he was found.

Safe Haven Rescue said Winston was given a bath, flea treatment, fresh food and water, and has since received his first vaccines and begun deworming treatment.

The rescue also took in two doodles over the weekend, according to the organization. One, a nearly 2-year-old dog now named Chappie, was being given away. Another, a 3-year-old goldendoodle named Kash, was surrendered after the owners said they had too many dogs.

The rescue said Kash is underweight and needs grooming and neutering.

In the middle of those rescues, the group said a local animal control officer asked for help with a heavily pregnant dog. Safe Haven Rescue said the dog, now named Sweet Caroline, was placed in foster care and gave birth the next morning.

According to the rescue, Sweet Caroline delivered 10 puppies, including seven males, two females and one stillborn.

Safe Haven Rescue said it is now low on funds and is asking for donations as it continues caring for the animals.

The rescue is located in Monticello, Mississippi and relies on support from the community to help them to continue helping animals. Please consider donating and making a difference.

You can reach them by phone at 912-674-0518 or email at [email protected] .

item.title: MEMA shares checklist to help Mississippians prepare for overnight storms - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Mississippi Emergency Management Agency is urging residents to prepare ahead of severe weather by reviewing a checklist focused on overnight storms.

In a storm safety graphic, MEMA encouraged people to charge their phones during the day, identify their safe spot in advance and turn weather alerts on loud.

The agency also advised residents to prepare that safe area with pillows and helmets, keep shoes nearby and make sure they have multiple ways to receive alerts.

MEMA said people should know their county, follow their local National Weather Service office and download the free MEMA app.

The checklist also reminds pet owners to keep a leash nearby in case they need to move quickly during severe weather.

Emergency officials have repeatedly warned that overnight storms can be especially dangerous because people may be asleep when warnings are issued. MEMA is encouraging Mississippians to make preparations before bad weather develops.

item.description:
NATCHEZ — Community leaders, business owners and prospective investors will gather Saturday for the 2026 Downtown Unlocked Real Estate Showcase, an event focused on economic development and opportunities in downtown Natchez.

Transportation assistance will be available for those who need it, organizers said.

The showcase is supported by several sponsors, including the Community Foundation for Mississippi, Concordia Bank & Trust Co., Bank of Franklin, Delta Bank and United Mississippi Bank, along with other community and in-kind partners.

Organizers said the event is designed to highlight investment opportunities and support continued revitalization efforts in downtown Natchez.

item.title: Claiborne County sheriff partners with MSU program to connect residents with jobs - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CLAIBORNE COUNTY – The Claiborne County Sheriff’s Office has partnered with Mississippi State University’s Career Horizons Project to help connect local residents with job opportunities, Sheriff Edward Goods announced.

Goods said the program is aimed at helping people affected by COVID-19 get back on their feet.

According to the sheriff’s office, opportunities are available for people ages 16 to 70, with both part-time and full-time positions offered for those who qualify.

The program includes job placement, job retention assistance, career counseling and support for people impacted by long COVID.

The sheriff encouraged anyone interested to stop by, apply and take the next step toward employment.

COLUMBUS – A 15-year-old boy remains in critical condition after officers found him collapsed in the roadway with a gunshot wound Thursday in Columbus, according to the Columbus Police Department.

Police said officers were in the area of 19th Street and 7th Avenue North on April 23 when they saw a male lying in the roadway.

The victim was identified as 15-year-old Messiah Harmon.

Police said Harmon was first taken to Baptist Memorial Hospital for treatment. Because of the severity of his injuries, he was later airlifted to another hospital, where he remains in critical condition.

The case remains under active investigation, and no additional details were immediately released.

Police said they are urging anyone with information about the shooting to contact the Columbus Police Department or Golden Triangle Crime Stoppers.

item.title: Driver pulled from submerged pickup after dramatic overnight rescue in Jones County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JONES COUNTY – A 20-year-old man was rescued early Sunday after his pickup truck crashed into a drainage canal and flipped upside down in water near the Glade community, according to the Jones County Sheriff’s Department.

Authorities said the crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. April 26 on Highway 15 South at the intersection of Whispering Sage Drive, an area commonly known as “The Flats.”

Deputy Stephen Graeser was the first to arrive and found a Toyota Tacoma upside down in a water-filled drainage canal, the sheriff’s department said. Investigators said the driver was injured and trapped inside the truck with only a small air pocket large enough for his head.

Additional deputies arrived along with crews from Glade Fire and Rescue, Powers Fire and Rescue and EMServ Ambulance Service, according to authorities.

The sheriff’s department said Graeser entered the water and tried to pry open the driver’s door. He was soon joined by Glade Fire Chief Charles Cromwell and Powers firefighter and emergency medical responder D.L. Gieger Jr.

Using a Halligan pry bar and battery-powered rescue spreaders, the three were able to force open the door and remove the driver from the truck, authorities said. The driver was then taken up the embankment to a backboard where EMS crews were waiting.

The driver, identified as Anselmo Mendez Jr., 20, was transported by EMServ to South Central Regional Medical Center in Laurel. Authorities said his injuries were believed to be non-life-threatening.

Investigators said the truck was traveling south on Highway 15 when it left the road, struck several large rocks at the base of a concrete bridge at Whispering Sage Drive and went airborne for about 60 feet. The truck then hit the bridge rail on the opposite side and flipped upside down into the water.

“Great job by all of the emergency responders who effected the rescue of Mr. Mendez from the sunken cab of his crashed pickup truck,” Sheriff Joe Berlin said in a statement.

Berlin said the rescue highlighted the importance of teamwork among first responders.

item.title: Body of missing Brandon teen recovered from lake - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
BRANDON — A 17-year-old Brandon resident was found dead Sunday after a search and rescue operation at a private lake near Marquette Road in Brandon.

The Brandon Police Department received a call around 2:38 p.m. Sunday reporting that Noah Lee Lambert, 17, of Brandon, had jumped from a height into the lake and could not be located by his friends.

Brandon police officers and firefighters responded and began immediate search and rescue efforts. They were assisted by Rankin County Sheriff’s Department deputies and dive rescue team using boats, divers and drones. Noah’s body was later recovered from the lake. His family has been notified.

The lake is located on private property with signs posted warning against trespassing. Local teens and young adults have been known to frequent the area over the years.

Noah was a sophomore at Brandon High School. The Rankin County School District will make grief counselors available to students and faculty affected by his death.

The Brandon Police Department extends its deepest condolences to Noah’s family, friends, classmates and all who knew him. Our thoughts and prayers are with them during this heartbreaking time, and we ask the community to respect the family’s privacy as they grieve.
